 4. Pursuant to the said F.I.R. Ramna Police Station Case No. 51 dated 15.6.2002 was registered which gave rise to G.R. Case No. 1687 of 2002. Petitioner along with 2 other accused persons were taken on police remand for 2 days by order dated 16.6.2002 but none of them made any confessional statement. Petitioner unsuccessfully moved the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka for bail in Metropolitan Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2686 of 2002 and thereafter obtained this rule. 

 5. Mr. A. Baset Majumder, learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that petitioner is a practising Advocate of this court who has been implicated in this case out of suspicion although he was not the filing Advocate on behalf of accused Ibrahim Miah and 2 others in Criminal 

 Miscellaneous Case No. 5690 of 2002 and that learned Advocate Syed Mizanur Rahman who preferred the application under Section 498 Cr. P.C. on behalf of the said accused Ibrahim Miah and 2 others has not been implicated in this case. The learned Advocate further submits that the 

 7. Since the alleged forgery has been perpetrated by forging the signatures of the learned Judges of this Court, we have called for the record of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 5690 of 2002 and pursuant thereto, the said record has been placed before us. We have perused the order dated 15.6.2002, by which, this Court directed the Registrar to lodge an F.I.R. against the petitioner and others. This Court observed "the conduct of Advocate Mr. Md. Nurul Islam Chowdhury and those Mr. Abul Khair and Mr. Abu Sayed evoked and found suspicion about their possible involvement in the perpetration of the forgery." 

 8. Since the learned Deputy Attorney General does not oppose the prayer for bail, - we are not inclined to make any observation touching the merit of the case. However, we would like to observe that the petitioner is not the filing Advocate of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 5690 of 2002 in which, accused Ibrahim Miah and others managed to secure a forged order of bail. We find that the petitioner is a practising Advocate of this Court and a diabetics patient. On consideration of the materials on record, we are of the view that there are not reasonable ground for believing that the petitioner has committed a non-bailable offence but that there are sufficient grounds for further enquiry into his guilt, he shall, pending such enquiry be admitted on bail under sub-Section (2) of Section 497 Cr. P.C.
